name: Yam Leaf Spot
description: A fungal disease causing leaf spots and blighting in yam. It reduces photosynthetic capacity, causes premature defoliation, and can significantly reduce tuber yield. It is one of the most common foliar diseases of yam in West Africa.
symptoms: Circular to irregular brown spots on leaves
Spots with yellow halos and dark margins
Spots coalescing to form large necrotic areas
Leaves turning yellow and dropping prematurely
Reduced vine growth and tuber bulking
causes: Colletotrichum gloeosporioides and Cercospora spp. fungi
Extended leaf wetness from rain or dew
Dense vine canopy with poor air circulation
treatments: Apply copper-based fungicides at first symptoms
Spray mancozeb or chlorothalonil at 10-14 day intervals
Remove and destroy severely infected leaves
prevention: Space yam mounds or ridges adequately
Provide good staking for vine trellising to improve air flow
Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest
Use disease-free yam setts for planting
